To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) agents do not learn relational tasks from reward alone but do learn them when trained to generate explanations, and (b) generating explanations can enable agents to overcome the tendency to fixate on features, to generalize from ambiguous data, and to perform meta-learning.

1) explanations help agents overcome the tendency to fixate on single dimensions, and 2) explanations can enable generalization from ambiguous training and meta-learning to perform causal interventions.

(a) learning to predict explanations of the world can help machine learning systems learn more efficiently, (b) learning to predict the explanations of the world helps machine learning systems to overcome the tendency to fixate on simplistic features, and (c) learning to predict and generate explanations of the world is a powerful principle for training machine learning systems to perform tasks that require learning causal structure and abstractions.
